transcript: Four days, he said. Rook stopped. Nobody said anything for a moment. Out in the field, a pigeon went up out of the thorn and clattered away. Gates rutted going out and not coming in, said Rook. Two carts, out. And the grass at the field gate is trodden flat on the inside and standing on the outside, because fifteen people leaving a field in the morning walk out of it in a bunch, and fifteen people coming into a field at dusk come in one at a time, looking about them. The throat had been open so many times that the sacking had come away from itself entirely, and the straw was out. Why not thee? And then stopped, and went slightly grey and said, Oh, it started ordinarily. Up on the bank, in the dark, the man who had spent the afternoon teaching four children how to be hurt by people sat with his back to the camp, and his face to the north, which was new, and which nobody mentioned, and which every single one of them had noticed.
